coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P23
names: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
record.summary: A landscaped lawn and plaza between Illinois Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, extending toward the Chase Center roundabout and next to a pavilion (not the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, which is about 800 m to the north-west); per this repository's own satellite trace, real landscaped/paved open land, delineated by this project's owner-directed real-gap-fragment method rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P23' among the parcels the Port of San Francisco will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date. SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery and the street/already-tracked-polygon-bounded gap computation, divided at owner-specified cross-sectional seams rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23 & P24'); SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left untracked as its own P-number pending further review.
notes.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (fragment 2, 19,181.78 sqm raw). The owner reviewed a 3-way width-scan split of that fragment (at its two real cross-sectional waists, lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then gave a precise construction: P23 is the north piece (piece2, the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (piece1, the plaza) that lies east of the seam where piece2's lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south.

milestones.text: Reported as the nearly 2-acre 'Mariposa Bayfront Park (P23/P24)', 'yet to be completed' and expected to be completed by the end of 2019 (SocketSite; the source does not say construction had started)

changes.text: The P23 map shape cited no sources; it now lists the OCII Dec 2019 Land Use Map, the OCII Sept 2023 transition presentation and SocketSite's April 2019 article, and its caveat names the Port as manager (per OCII's deck) and notes SocketSite's name 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' for the combined P23/P24 area. The April 2019 milestone said under construction; SocketSite says only that the space had 'yet to be completed' and was expected to finish by the end of 2019, so it is now planned. The summary said the lawn is north of the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, which is about 800 m to the north-west; it now says it is between Illinois St and Terry A. Francois Blvd next to a different pavilion. 'Already managed by the Port' became 'will manage' to match the deck. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural, and the OCII deck title no longer says 'CAC Item 2'.

open_questions: The April 2019 SocketSite article names the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' -- not to be confused with Mariposa Park, OCII's own official P26 per its current open-space page (a separate, larger playground park at Mariposa and Owens streets; see this repo's mission_bay_p26_interchange_wedge record's own open_questions for a related P26 label conflict). Not reconciled here, only noted so the two 'Mariposa'-named places aren't conflated.

No source names this specific lawn/plaza or gives its own construction date beyond the April 2019 under-construction report; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already Port-managed by that date, which is an upper bound, not a build date.

It sits adjacent to the Chase Center arena (opened September 2019, per this repo's own record 8722025) and to the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St area, but no source ties this landscaped area's own completion to either project.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P23' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P23 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).

The April 2019 SocketSite article says only that the P23/P24 open space had 'yet to be completed' and was expected to be completed by the end of 2019; it does not say construction had started, so the 2019-04 milestone is 'planned', not 'under construction'.
